 HIGH COURT OF KERALA, ERNAKULAM - 682 031.
 (SHO, ADOOR POLICE STATION, PATHANAMTHITTA)

SRI. PRASANTH M.P., PP THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.07.2025,
THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NO. 8123 OF 2025  2  2025:KER:509
This bail application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.1312/2025 of Adoor Police Station,
Pathanamthitta District; registered for the offences punishable under Section 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The prosecution case is that, the accused had, with the intent to make unlawful gain, by deceit,
lured the defacto complainant into investing Rs.5,00,000/- with a financial institution by name M/s.Maxvalue Credits and Investments Ltd., by falsely promising to return double of the invested amount and thereafter failed to pay any amount and even refused to return the amounts deposited,
and thereby committed the above offences.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioners have BAIL APPL. NO. 8123 OF 2025 2025:KER:50971 been falsely arrayed as accused and that they have no involvement in the alleged crime.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are serious in nature and custodial interrogation is essential.

sentences.text: 7. Defacto complainant alleges that an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- was invested with the company by name 'Maxvalue Credits and Investments Ltd.,' for the purpose of purchasing equity shares of the said company.
The first accused is the former Branch Manager, the second accused is the present Branch Manager and the third accused is the Chairman of the aforesaid company

. Annexure-A3 is the share application form submitted by the defacto complainant while Annexure-A2 indicates that there was a Rights Issue of the company and the defacto complainant was allotted 25000 shares for a total value of Rs.5,00,000/-.
8.

Since the defacto complainant has apparently invested in purchasing equity shares in a company,
prima facie, he cannot seek refund of the amount or allege that the amount has not been doubled as expected by him.
The said concept is contrary to the principles of Company Law.
In such a view of the matter, it is evident that this is a fit case where petitioners should be protected with an order of pre-arrest bail.

9. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1], it was held that, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by BAIL APPL. NO. 8123 OF 2025 2025:KER:50971 considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed are all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.

10. On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this Court is of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not required and they are entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.

11. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) In the event of the petitioners being arrested in Crime No.1312/2025 of Adoor Police Station, Pathanamthitta District; they shall be released on bail on each of them executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(b) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation if they are so required in writing and shall co- operate with the investigation.
(c) Petitioners shall not destroy or tamper with the evidence or intimidate or threaten or contact the defacto complainant.
(d) Petitioners shall not commit any other similar offences while they are on bail.
BAIL APPL. NO. 8123 OF 2025 2025:KER:50971

In case of violation of any of the above conditions,
